In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is false but (R) is true
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
C) (A) is true but (R) is false
D) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand the trans-effect in square planar complexes. The trans-effect is the ability of a coordinated ligand to direct an incoming nucleophilic substitution to the coordination position trans (opposite) to itself. The trans-directing series gives: $\text{Cl}^- > \text{NH}_3$.
Step 2: Analyze the synthesis of cisplatin from $[\text{PtCl}_4]^{2-}$. When the first $\text{NH}_3$ replaces a $\text{Cl}^-$, the mono-substituted intermediate $[\text{PtCl}_3(\text{NH}_3)]^-$ is formed. In this intermediate, the two chloride ligands trans to each other have a stronger trans-directing effect than the ammine ligand. Therefore, the incoming second $\text{NH}_3$ ligand selectively replaces a chloride ligand that is trans to another chloride, placing the two $\text{NH}_3$ ligands mutually cis to each other. This yields $cis\text{-}[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ (cisplatin).
Step 3: Relate (A) and (R). Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is true, and (R) provides the exact theoretical and kinetic explanation for (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the spectrochemical series and molecular orbital interactions:
Statement I: Halide ions are positioned at the weak-field end of the spectrochemical series because their filled $p$-orbitals act as $\pi$-donors toward metal $d$-orbitals, which destabilizes the $t_{2g}$ orbitals and decreases $\Delta_o$.
Statement II: Ligands like $\text{CO}$ and $\text{CN}^-$ are positioned at the strong-field end of the spectrochemical series because they possess low-lying empty $\pi^*$ orbitals that act as $\pi$-acceptors, which stabilizes the $t_{2g}$ orbitals and dramatically increases $\Delta_o$.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
C) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
D) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Halide ions ($	ext{I}^-, 	ext{Br}^-, 	ext{Cl}^-, 	ext{F}^-$) have filled valence $p$-orbitals perpendicular to the metal-ligand $\sigma$-axis. These filled orbitals overlap with the metal $t_{2g}$ orbitals in a $\pi$-donor fashion. The resulting antibonding $\pi^*$ molecular orbitals (predominantly metal $t_{2g}$ in character) are raised in energy closer to the $e_g^*$ level, significantly reducing the energy gap $\Delta_o$. Hence, $\pi$-donor ligands produce weak crystal fields. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Ligands like $\text{CO}$ and $\text{CN}^-$ have vacant low-energy $\pi^*$ molecular orbitals. Overlap between the filled metal $t_{2g}$ orbitals and these empty ligand $\pi^*$ orbitals ($\pi$-backbonding) lowers the energy of the bonding $t_{2g}$ molecular orbitals. This increases the energy separation $\Delta_o$ between $t_{2g}$ and $e_g^*$. Hence, $\pi$-acceptor ligands produce very strong crystal fields. Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Which of the following coordination entities exhibit optical isomerism (chirality)?
(1) $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$
(2) $cis\text{-}[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$
(3) $trans\text{-}[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$
(4) $[\text{Cr}(\text{ox})_3]^{3-}$
(5) $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$
Select the correct combination:
options: B) (1), (2), and (4) only
C) (2), (3), and (5) only
D) (1) and (4) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Examine (1) $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$. It is of the type $[\text{M}(\text{AA})_3]$. It adopts a propeller-like $D_3$ symmetry that lacks any plane of symmetry ($\sigma$) or center of inversion ($i$). It is chiral and exists as $\Delta$ (dextro) and $\Lambda$ (laevo) enantiomers. Hence, (1) exhibits optical isomerism.
Step 2: Examine (2) $cis\text{-}[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$. It is of type $cis\text{-}[\text{M}(\text{AA})_2\text{b}_2]$. It possesses only a $C_2$ axis and lacks an improper axis of rotation ($S_n$). It is chiral and exists as a pair of enantiomers. Hence, (2) exhibits optical isomerism.
Step 3: Examine (3) $trans\text{-}[\text{Co}(\text{en})_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$. It possesses three mirror planes and an inversion center ($i$). It is achiral and optically inactive. It does not exhibit optical isomerism.
Step 4: Examine (4) $[\text{Cr}(\text{ox})_3]^{3-}$. Like $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$, it has three bidentate oxalate chelate rings in an octahedral arrangement ($D_3$ symmetry), making it chiral and optically active. Hence, (4) exhibits optical isomerism.
Step 5: Examine (5) $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$. This is a four-coordinate square planar complex. All square planar complexes have a horizontal plane of symmetry (the molecular plane itself) and are achiral. Hence, only (1), (2), and (4) exhibit optical isomerism.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Chelates containing five-membered rings formed by saturated bidentate ligands like ethane-1,2-diamine are generally more thermodynamically stable than those forming four-membered or seven-membered chelate rings.
Reason (R): Five-membered saturated chelate rings feature near-ideal tetrahedral bond angles ($109.5^\circ$) at carbon and nitrogen atoms with negligible Bayer angle strain, whereas four-membered rings suffer from severe bond angle strain and seven-membered rings experience unfavorable conformational entropy penalties.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is true but (R) is false
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
C) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Chelate stability strongly depends on ring size. In general, for saturated chelating ligands without conjugated double bonds (such as ethylenediamine), five-membered rings form the most thermodynamically stable complexes (e.g., $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$). For conjugated ligands (like acetylacetonate), six-membered rings are also exceptionally stable. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). A four-membered chelate ring forces bond angles at the coordinating atoms to compress below $90^\circ$, producing severe ring strain. Seven-membered rings have greater conformational flexibility, incurring a substantial entropic penalty upon ring closure without compensatory enthalpy gain. In contrast, five-membered saturated rings achieve nearly staggered, strain-free conformations with minimal angle distortion. Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I (Octahedral Complex) with List II ($d$-electron configuration, CFSE, and spin-only magnetic moment $\mu_{\text{s}}$):

List I
A. $[\text{Mn}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$
B. $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$
C. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$
D. $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$

List II
I. $t_{2g}^3 e_g^0$, $\text{CFSE} = -1.2\Delta_o$, $\mu_{\text{s}} \approx 3.87\text{ BM}$
II. $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$, $\text{CFSE} = -2.4\Delta_o + 2P$, $\mu_{\text{s}} = 0\text{ BM}$
III. $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$, $\text{CFSE} = 0.0\Delta_o$, $\mu_{\text{s}} \approx 5.92\text{ BM}$
IV. $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$, $\text{CFSE} = -0.4\Delta_o$, $\mu_{\text{s}} \approx 4.90\text{ BM}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III
B) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
C) A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
D) A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match $[\text{Mn}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ (A). $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ is $3d^5$. Water is a weak field ligand ($\Delta_o < P$), giving a high-spin configuration $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$. $\text{CFSE} = 3(-0.4) + 2(0.6) = 0.0\Delta_o$. With $5$ unpaired electrons, $\mu_{\text{s}} = \sqrt{5(7)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92\text{ BM}$: A matches III.
Step 2: Match $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ (B). $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ is $3d^3$. Configuration is $t_{2g}^3 e_g^0$. $\text{CFSE} = 3(-0.4) = -1.2\Delta_o$. With $3$ unpaired electrons, $\mu_{\text{s}} = \sqrt{3(5)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87\text{ BM}$: B matches I.
Step 3: Match $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ (C). $\text{Co}^{3+}$ is $3d^6$. Ammonia is a strong field ligand for $\text{Co}^{3+}$, producing low-spin $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$. $\text{CFSE} = -2.4\Delta_o + 2P$. With $0$ unpaired electrons, $\mu_{\text{s}} = 0\text{ BM}$ (diamagnetic): C matches II.
Step 4: Match $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ (D). $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ is $3d^6$. Water is weak field, giving high-spin $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$. $\text{CFSE} = 4(-0.4) + 2(0.6) = -0.4\Delta_o$. With $4$ unpaired electrons, $\mu_{\text{s}} = \sqrt{4(6)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90\text{ BM}$: D matches IV. Hence, the match is A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding four-coordinate complexes of heavier transition elements:
Statement I: All four-coordinate complexes of divalent palladium ($\text{Pd}^{2+}$, $4d^8$) and divalent platinum ($\text{Pt}^{2+}$, $5d^8$) are square planar and diamagnetic, regardless of whether the coordinated ligands are halides or strong field ligands like cyanide.
Statement II: Moving down a triad from $3d$ to $4d$ and $5d$ transition metals, the crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta$) increases significantly (by approximately $30-50\%$), such that $\Delta$ exceeds the pairing energy ($P$) even with weak-field ligands.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
B) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
D) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. For $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ($3d^8$), $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ is tetrahedral and paramagnetic because $\text{Cl}^-$ cannot overcome pairing energy. However, for its heavier congeners $\text{Pd}^{2+}$ and $\text{Pt}^{2+}$, $[\text{PdCl}_4]^{2-}$ and $[\text{PtCl}_4]^{2-}$ are square planar ($dsp^2$) and diamagnetic. In fact, virtually all four-coordinate $\text{Pd(II)}$ and $\text{Pt(II)}$ complexes are square planar and diamagnetic. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. As principal quantum number increases from $3d$ to $4d$ to $5d$, the $d$-orbitals are more diffuse and extend further into space, interacting far more strongly with ligand orbitals. Consequently, the crystal field splitting $\Delta$ increases by roughly $40\%$ from $3d$ to $4d$ and another $25\%$ from $4d$ to $5d$. Concurrently, the larger orbital volume decreases inter-electronic repulsion, lowering the pairing energy $P$. Thus, $\Delta > P$ is universally satisfied for $4d$ and $5d$ metals, forcing electron pairing and favoring low-spin square planar geometry. Statement II is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
A coordination compound $\text{X}$ having the empirical formula $\text{CrCl}_3 \cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$ undergoes the following reactions:
(i) An aqueous solution of $0.01\text{ mol}$ of $\text{X}$ requires exactly $20\text{ mL}$ of $1.0\text{ M } \text{AgNO}_3$ solution for complete precipitation of chloride ions.
(ii) Dehydration of $0.01\text{ mol}$ of solid $\text{X}$ over concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ results in a mass loss of $0.18\text{ g}$.
Based on these observations, which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding compound $\text{X}$?
options: A) The secondary valency of chromium in compound $\text{X}$ is $6$
B) Compound $\text{X}$ exhibits geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism
C) Its aqueous solution exhibits an electrical conductivity corresponding to a $1:2$ electrolyte
D) The IUPAC name of compound $\text{X}$ is pentaaquachloridochromium(III) chloride monohydrate
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the moles of ionisable chloride ions per mole of complex. Moles of $\text{Ag}^+$ consumed = $V \times M = 0.020\text{ L} \times 1.0\text{ mol/L} = 0.02\text{ mol}$. Since $0.01\text{ mol}$ of $\text{X}$ reacts with $0.02\text{ mol}$ of $\text{AgNO}_3$, there are $\frac{0.02}{0.01} = 2$ ionisable chloride ions per formula unit in the outer sphere ($\text{Cl}_2$).
Step 2: Calculate the moles of water of crystallization per mole of complex. Moles of water lost = $\frac{0.18\text{ g}}{18\text{ g/mol}} = 0.01\text{ mol}$. Since $0.01\text{ mol}$ of $\text{X}$ loses $0.01\text{ mol}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, there is exactly $1$ water molecule of crystallization outside the coordination sphere ($\cdot \text{H}_2\text{O}$).
Step 3: Deduce the coordination formula. The remaining five water molecules and one chloride ion are coordinated to $\text{Cr}^{3+}$: $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2 \cdot \text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Step 4: Evaluate each statement:
- Secondary valency is the coordination number: $5$ aqua $+ 1$ chlorido = $6$. (Correct)
- IUPAC name: pentaaquachloridochromium(III) chloride monohydrate. (Correct)
- Ionisation: $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5\text{Cl}]^{2+} + 2\text{Cl}^-$, which is a $1:2$ electrolyte. (Correct)
- Geometrical isomerism: The complex cation is of the type $[\text{Ma}_5\text{b}]$. Octahedral complexes of type $[\text{Ma}_5\text{b}]$ have only one spatial arrangement and CANNOT exhibit cis-trans geometrical isomerism. Therefore, statement D is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): An aqueous solution of the titanium(III) coordination complex $[\text{Ti}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ exhibits a distinctive purple/violet color.
Reason (R): The complex absorbs light in the blue-green region of visible radiation (wavelength $\approx 498\text{ nm}$) to promote a single $d$-electron from the $t_{2g}$ level to the $e_g$ level, and the transmitted light corresponds to the complementary purple/violet color.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is true but (R) is false
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
C) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
D) (A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Titanium is element $22$; $\text{Ti}^{3+}$ has the valence configuration $[\text{Ar}]\,3d^1$. In $[\text{Ti}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$, the single $d$-electron resides in the lower $t_{2g}$ set: $t_{2g}^1 e_g^0$. Solutions of this complex are famously purple-violet in color. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). The crystal field splitting $\Delta_o$ for $[\text{Ti}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ is approximately $20,000\text{ cm}^{-1}$ ($240\text{ kJ/mol}$), which corresponds to the absorption of light at a wavelength of $\lambda = \frac{hc}{\Delta_o} \approx 498\text{ nm}$ (in the blue-green region). When white light passes through the solution, the blue-green light is absorbed to excite the electron from $t_{2g}$ to $e_g$. The transmitted light, being deficient in blue-green, appears purple-violet (its complementary color). Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).
